newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: U.N. team reviews peace needs in Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: U.N. team reviews peace needs in Sierra Leone.

text.p: A seven-member United Nations team held talks with Sierra Leone's president on Friday as part of efforts to assess peacekeeping needs after the November 30 peace deal between the government and rebels, officials said.

"The team will leave Freetown for the regional capitals, Bo, Kenema, Makeni for on-the-spot assessment before they return to New York to report to the U.N. secretary-general," President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah's special advisor, Sheka Mansaray, said.
Mansaray told reporters the government expected a peacekeeping force to be sent to Sierra Leone.
U.N. special envoy Berhanu Dinka said the mission, which would also travel to Ivory Coast for talks with Revolutionary United Front rebel leader Foday Sankoh, would return to New York on January 6.
"The peace process in Sierra Leone is now at an advanced stage. A lot of homework has been done and the chances of the process succeeding is very good indeed," Dinka said.

The government and rebels signed the November 30 peace deal in Ivory Coast, which helped mediate. The rebels took up arms in 1991. The war killed at least 10,000 people, according to official estimates.
